name: Brothy Vegetarian Edamame & Potato Succotash with Toasted Flatbread

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium yellow potatoes
3 red bell peppers
6 sticks celery
1 ½ small pkgs grape tomatoes
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley

instructions.primary_message: Peel and small dice potatoes; transfer to a large bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers; add to the bowl with the potato.
Trim and cut celery crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, peel, halve, and thinly slice onions.
Once the pot is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onion and spices to the pot; cook, stirring often, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp butter, unsalted
1 ½ tsp paprika
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper
¾ tsp thyme, dried

instructions.primary_message: Add veggies, broth, edamame, corn, and sugar to the pot with the onion. Stir to combine the succotash and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, about 10 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1065 ml chicken or vegetable broth
3 cups edamame
1 ½ cups frozen corn
1 ½ tsp brown sugar

instructions.primary_message: While the succotash is cooking, halve tomatoes and place in the reserved bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes and set aside.
Toast flatbread if desired (optional), then slice into wedges.
When the succotash is done, add tomatoes, parsley, and cream to the pot; stir to combine and remove from heat.
To serve, divide succotash between bowls and enjoy with warm flatbread on the side!
